One long fall, from cloud to coral.

44 rivers.590 km of coast.One long fall.

Kerala is only 35 to 120 km wide. Mountains, rivers, rice fields and sea sit a few hours apart, and all of it runs downhill.

Tea country. Hand-picked slopes in the cool Western Ghats, worked by families who have done it for generations.

Tea pickers, Munnar

Forest and spice hills. Elephants live in the reserve and in village life; a mahout and his elephant are a daily sight.

A mahout and his elephant

Where the hills hand the river over to the plains. The falls are loudest in the monsoon.

Athirappilly Falls

Rice is grown here below sea level, behind earth bunds. You travel between the fields by boat.

A boatman, Alappuzha

Fishermen, Chinese fishing nets in Kochi and red cliffs at Varkala. The fall ends here.

A fisherman, Kerala coast

When to come

MonsoonOnamTheyyamWinter sun

June to September

The rains arrive in June. Rice turns bright green, waterfalls roar, and it is the traditional season for Ayurveda.

August to September

Kerala's harvest festival. Flower carpets fill doorways, feasts are served on banana leaves, and long snake boats race.

November to May

In northern villages a performer becomes a god by firelight. It is a ritual, not a show, and visitors are welcome to watch.

December to February

Dry, bright and mild. The best weeks for beaches, hills and long days on the water.
